Τοιουτοσὶ δέ πως, ὁ βίον μὲν ἔχων τὸν κοσμικὸν, ἐπιεικείας γε μὴν τῆς ἄλλης καὶ ἀγάπης τῆς εἰς Θεὸν οὐκ εἰσάπαν ἠμοιρηκώς· ὁ γὰρ τοιοῦτος, οὐ τοῖς ἐπιγείοις παντελῶς ἐνδέδεται, καὶ ἐνιζάνει τοῖς κάτω, μεμελέτηκε δέ πως καὶ τὰ ἄνω φρονεῖν, καὶ εὐδοκιμεῖν ἔσθ' ὅτε, πρὸς τὰ ἄνω διαπηδῶν καὶ τῶν ἐπιγείων ὑπεριπτάμενος. pass_a_gloss: §25 dual gloss: ἀναθρῴσκω / leap-up · ἑσπέρα / evening · βάπτισμα / baptism … Pass A ≠ Pass B. Theme: Leaping insects; evening wash types baptism at age-end.
pass_b_english: Cyril: ...ones, locust and caterpillar and the resembling these, through at least the well-strong, as to be able to leap-up, and least to love-to-dwell in the below, and to be lifted often unto the on-high, and to leap-through easily. And somehow such is the one having the worldly life, yet not altogether without-share of fairness and of love unto God; for such a one has not been bound altogether to the earthly things, yet has somehow practiced also to think the above, and is well-reputed sometimes, leaping-through toward the above and flying-over the earthly. And the one touching the unclean and having been defiled must wash-out the garment; and toward evening, he says, he will be clean, signaling very well the mystery of Christ, through whom we have been cleansed, enriching the release through the holy baptism, according to the season of his sojourn, having become as it were toward evening, that is, with the present age already creeping-through unto an end. Or do we not say the Word of God has become human in last seasons?

Cyril: And profane also the law says otherwise will be the one somehow touching either of a wild beast or of another unclean animal; and he said thus: 'And every one who walks upon hands in all the beasts which walk upon four, unclean they are for you. Everyone touching their carcasses will be unclean until evening; and the one lifting of their carcasses will wash his garments and be unclean until evening. Unclean these are for you. And these unclean for you from the creeping ones upon the earth: the weasel, and the mouse, and the land-crocodile, shrew-mouse, and chameleon, and gecko, and lizard, and mole. These unclean for you from all the creeping ones upon the earth. Everyone touching them having died will be unclean until evening. And every upon which if there should fall from them having died, unclean it will be, from every wooden vessel or garment' (Leviticus 11:21–32) (1 Corinthians 10:11)
